```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
library(fpp3)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4
)
source("lab_submission.R")

lab_meta <- list(id = "lab06", title = "Benchmark Forecasts")
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1 = "Seasonal naïve for quarterly Beer forecasts uses which lag?",
  q2 = "Drift forecasts are a straight line with slope equal to:",
  q3 = "Which method looks most reasonable for Beer and why (1–2 sentences)?"
)
```

## What you will do

Open this file and click **Run Document**. Packages: `learnr`, `fpp3`.
Exercise chunks run when you click Run Code. They are not knitted in one pass.

## Fit benchmarks
```{r bench-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=14}
library(fpp3)
train <- aus_production |> filter_index(. ~ "2005 Q4")
fit <- train |>
  model(
    Mean = MEAN(Beer),
    Naive = NAIVE(Beer),
    SNaive = SNAIVE(Beer),
    Drift = RW(Beer ~ drift())
  )
fc <- fit |> forecast(h = "8 quarters")
fc |> autoplot(aus_production)
```

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("Lag 4 (same quarter last year)", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Lag 1 only"),
  answer("Lag 12"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q2}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q2"]],
  answer("Average change between first and last observation", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Always zero"),
  answer("The seasonal index only"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q3}
question_text(
  lab_prompts[["q3"]],
  open_answer(),
  placeholder = "e.g. SNAIVE because strong seasonality …",
  trim = TRUE
)
```

```{r submit-server, context="server"}
output$download_txt <- shiny::downloadHandler(
  filename = function() lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
  content = function(file) {
    write_lab_submission(
      path = file,
      name = input$student_name,
      lab_id = lab_meta$id,
      lab_title = lab_meta$title,
      state = learnr::get_tutorial_state(),
      prompts = lab_prompts
    )
  }
)
```
